learningObjectives: Link TemplateInstances to a specific Requirement inside a RequirementSet.
Create and link an ExecutionList to Requirements.

elements.text: As covered in AS1, we use ExecutionLists and RequirementSets to run tests and get a project-level overview. Here we build an ExecutionList for the Template-generated TestCases from this course, so results and any bugs get reported properly.

elements.title: 3 ways to create an ExecutionList
items: Click Create Object in the EXECUTIONLIST tab of the Ribbon.
Right-click the ExecutionList folder → Create Execution from the Context Menu.
Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E.

elements.text: ExecutionLists always live inside an ExecutionList Folder. You can't create one directly at the Execution root — first create an ExecutionList Folder under the root Execution folder, then create the ExecutionList inside that folder.

elements.description: The auto-generated folder holding every TestCase a Template produced. Shown as a teal/cyan folder icon with a capital "I". This is the object you drag as a whole — onto a Requirement and onto an ExecutionList — never individual TestCases from inside it.

A RequirementSet is a hollow/outline orange triangle — a container that groups related Requirements (e.g. "WebShop Frontend"). An individual Requirement is a solid/filled orange triangle (e.g. "Log in", under Customer tasks). They look similar at a glance, but only the filled triangle is the correct drop target for linking TemplateInstances at requirement level.
A green arrow/chevron icon, visually distinct from the TemplateInstances and Requirement icons — makes the Execution section easy to spot in the Navigation pane.

elements.text: Drag and drop the WHOLE TemplateInstance folder onto the ExecutionList — not individual TestCases. If the folder itself is linked, it's much easier to synchronize when the Template later changes: synchronization is manually triggered from the ExecutionList ribbon, and every ExecutionList linked to that folder updates automatically.

elements.title: Link TemplateInstances to a Requirement (Exercise 6a)
items: Navigate to the Requirements section and select the project's Requirements folder.
Expand the target RequirementSet and drill down to the specific Requirement (e.g. Customer tasks → "Log in").
Drag and drop the whole TemplateInstance folder onto that individual Requirement — the filled triangle, not the outline RequirementSet folder — to link them.

elements.title: Prepare before linking
items: Set the Template's WorkState to COMPLETED before linking the TemplateInstances to the ExecutionList and RequirementSet.
If TemplateInstances were already linked earlier, set the WorkState to COMPLETED now and then re-Instantiate.
Link the TemplateInstance folder to the RequirementSet as well — this populates results data into the requirement and gives a full coverage overview.
Link the ExecutionList to the appropriate RequirementSet via drag and drop.
Run the ExecutionList and review results/errors in detail.

elements.text: ExecutionState and CoverageSpecified are NOT columns in the Execution section — they appear on the RequirementSet/Requirement once the ExecutionList has been linked to it, i.e. in the Requirements section.

rows: Result of executed TestCases, factoring in risk, leading to a risk-based coverage statement.
What percentage of the overall project risk has been covered.

elements.text: These two columns feed directly into status reports/dashboards, giving developers exact information about which step failed and what the error message was.

examPitfalls.title: Linking individual TestCases instead of the whole TemplateInstance folder
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Learners drag single TestCases onto the ExecutionList one by one.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Drag and drop the entire TemplateInstance folder onto the ExecutionList for easier maintenance — synchronization then updates every linked ExecutionList automatically when the Template changes.

examPitfalls.title: Linking to ExecutionList/RequirementSet before WorkState is COMPLETED
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates link TemplateInstances to an ExecutionList while the Template's WorkState is still in progress.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set the WorkState to COMPLETED first. If already linked, set to COMPLETED and then re-Instantiate.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing ExecutionState with CoverageSpecified
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates mix up which column shows pass/fail risk-based results vs. overall risk coverage percentage.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ExecutionState = risk-based result of the executed TestCases. CoverageSpecified = percentage of overall project risk covered.

examPitfalls.title: Placing ExecutionState/CoverageSpecified in the Execution section
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume ExecutionState and CoverageSpecified are columns on the ExecutionList itself, in the Execution section.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: These columns live on the RequirementSet/Requirement, in the Requirements section — they populate there once the ExecutionList is linked to the RequirementSet, not on the ExecutionList itself.

examPitfalls.title: Dropping the TemplateInstance folder on the RequirementSet instead of the Requirement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates drag the TemplateInstance folder onto the RequirementSet (outline triangle) instead of drilling down to the specific Requirement (filled triangle) it belongs to.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Expand the RequirementSet and link at the individual Requirement level — that's what produces accurate per-requirement coverage data.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to create an ExecutionList directly at the Execution root
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates look for a way to create an ExecutionList straight under the root Execution folder.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: First create an ExecutionList Folder under the root Execution folder, then create the ExecutionList inside that folder.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE are valid ways to create an ExecutionList in Tosca?

options.text: Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E.
Click Create Object in the EXECUTIONLIST tab of the Ribbon.
Rename a TestSheet to 'ExecutionList'.
Right-click the ExecutionList folder → Create Execution.

practiceQuiz.hint: One ribbon button, one context-menu action, one keyboard shortcut.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ExecutionLists are created via the Ribbon's Create Object button, the folder's right-click Create Execution option, or the Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E shortcut. Renaming a TestSheet does nothing. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is it best practice to drag the whole TemplateInstance folder onto an ExecutionList, instead of individual TestCases?

options.text: It's easier to maintain — synchronizing the folder automatically updates every linked ExecutionList when the Template changes.
It automatically sets the WorkState to COMPLETED.
It runs the tests faster.
Tosca does not allow linking individual TestCases at all.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about maintenance and synchronization, not speed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Linking the whole TemplateInstance folder means a manually triggered synchronization (from the ExecutionList ribbon) updates every ExecutionList linked to that folder — far less maintenance than tracking individual TestCases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before linking TemplateInstances to an ExecutionList and RequirementSet, what must be true of the Template?

options.text: Its WorkState must be set to COMPLETED.
It must be converted back to a plain TestCase.
It must have zero Conditions set.
Its linked TestSheet must be deleted.

practiceQuiz.hint: If already linked and not yet completed, you'd need to re-Instantiate after fixing this.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The WorkState must be COMPLETED before linking. If TemplateInstances were already linked earlier, set the WorkState to COMPLETED and then re-Instantiate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the CoverageSpecified column show in the Requirements section?

options.text: The pass/fail result of each individual TestCase.
The license expiration date.
What percentage of the overall project risk has been covered.
The number of TestSteps in the ExecutionList.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about risk coverage percentage, not individual results — and it's not shown on the ExecutionList itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CoverageSpecified shows what percentage of the overall project risk has been covered, useful for status reports and dashboards. It appears on the RequirementSet/Requirement in the Requirements section once the ExecutionList is linked, not in the Execution section. ExecutionState shows the risk-based result of executed TestCases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In Exercise 6a, where should you drop the TemplateInstance folder to link it correctly for per-requirement coverage?

options.text: Directly onto the RequirementSet folder (outline triangle icon).
Onto the individual Requirement inside the RequirementSet (filled triangle icon).
Onto the root Requirements folder.
Onto the ExecutionList folder.

practiceQuiz.hint: Look for the filled triangle, not the outline one.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A RequirementSet is a hollow/outline triangle that just groups Requirements. Linking must happen on the individual Requirement (filled triangle) — e.g. "Log in" — to get accurate per-requirement coverage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must already exist before you can create an ExecutionList in the Execution section?

options.text: A completed RequirementSet.
An ExecutionList Folder under the root Execution folder.
A Template with zero Conditions.
Nothing — ExecutionLists can be created directly at the Execution root.

practiceQuiz.rationale: ExecutionLists always live inside an ExecutionList Folder. You must create that folder under the root Execution folder first, then create the ExecutionList inside it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Condition, what does the operator "==" mean?

options.text: Equal to
Not Equal to
AND
OR

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the default operator Tosca shows when you first drag an Instance into the Condition column.
practiceQuiz.rationale: "==" means the element must equal the given value — it's the default logical statement Tosca shows for a Condition. "!=" is the not-equal operator.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the purpose of Conditions in Tosca?

options.text: To give an accurate Status Report of the RequirementSet completion
To instruct Tosca on when to use, or not to use, certain TestStepFolders, TestSteps or TestStepValues
To instruct Tosca on which TestSheet to run
To instruct Tosca on when to use, or not to use, certain RequirementSet

practiceQuiz.hint: Conditions work at the Template's internal step level, not at the Requirement or TestSheet level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conditions let ONE Template cover multiple test paths by telling Tosca which TestStepFolders, TestSteps, or TestStepValues to include or skip for a given TestCase — avoiding the need for separate, competing Templates.
